lines.trans: Is your wrist all right?
It will heal. Seung-chan, since I am grateful to you, I will pay off thirty thousand won more.
Senior, you should pay fifty thousand won. That was not even an ordinary sedan.
Fine. Come to my desk tomorrow morning. I will withdraw the cash for you.
Senior, are you heading home?
Of course I am going home.
Where do you live?
It used to be Heukseok-dong, and soon I am moving to Dongtan. Why?
I was just wondering if there is any man you like.
Once spring comes, traffic gets jammed, so I always want to get out of Yeouido.
Hey, Baek Seung-chan, why are you asking me all these questions anyway?
Because you told me to ask whether I knew or did not know.

괜찮다.gloss: to be fine; to be okay

meanings.en: to be fine; to be okay; to be alright
meanings.note: Used to reassure someone, decline an offer politely, or say something is acceptable.

examples.trans: I'm really fine.
Is it okay if we meet tomorrow?

meanings.en: to become okay, to get better
meanings.note: Compound of 괜찮다 and -아/어지다.

examples.trans: It will get better soon.
It will get better soon. (2)

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Native Korean expression of thanks; 고마워요 is warm and polite.

examples.trans: Thank you so much for helping me.
Thank you always.
There are thirty thousand here.
Altogether, it is thirty thousand people.

meanings.note: Bound noun used with Sino-Korean numbers to state prices in South Korean won.

examples.trans: I only have a thousand won.
That is ten thousand won in total.

meanings.note: Used before adjectives or verbs.

examples.trans: Please give me a little more.
It's further away.
Let's pay off together today.
I worked hard to pay off yesterday too.

meanings.note: Used for giving things to someone of equal or lower status.

examples.trans: I gave a gift.
Please give me some water.

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.
There are fifty thousand here.
Altogether, it is fifty thousand people.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun for something near the speaker; often contracted to 이거 in speech.

examples.trans: Did you film this too?
How much is this?
Did you hear about this ordinary?
I was busy today because of ordinary.
Did you hear about this passenger car even?
I was busy today because of passenger car even.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.
Did you hear about this tomorrow?
I was busy today because of tomorrow.

meanings.note: Short for 아침밥

examples.trans: I woke up early in the morning.
Did you eat breakfast?
There are no seats.
It's my seat.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: Contrasted with 신용카드 (credit card).

examples.trans: I will pay in cash.
There is no cash in my wallet.

meanings.note: Primary everyday meaning.
Used at a bank or ATM for taking out cash.

examples.trans: I withdrew money at the bank.
I am looking for my keys.

놓다.gloss: to put, to place, to leave

meanings.en: to put, to place, to leave
meanings.note: Often used as an auxiliary verb to indicate leaving something in a certain state.

examples.trans: Please place it on the desk.
I left the door open.
I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그러면.

examples.trans: Then let's meet tomorrow.
Then we're at the same company!

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for location.

examples.trans: Where is the restroom?
Where are you right now?

meanings.note: Indicates that something will happen in a very short time.

examples.trans: The bus will arrive soon.
I will contact you again soon.
Did you hear about this moving?
I was busy today because of moving.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.

meanings.en: to like, to be fond of
meanings.note: Takes an object marked with 을/를.

examples.trans: What kind of food do you like?
I like listening to music.
Did you hear about this gentleman, man?
I was busy today because of gentleman, man.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.
Cherry blossoms bloom in spring.
It will be spring soon.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Short for 자동차.

examples.trans: This is my father's car.
I parked the car in the parking lot.
I want to gets backed up, so right now.
How about trying to gets backed up, so together tomorrow?
I want to leave right now.
How about trying to leave together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Auxiliary adjective attached to a verb stem with -고 (-고 싶다).

examples.trans: I want to go to Korea.
I want to drink a cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Casual exclamation used to call someone younger or a close friend.

examples.trans: Hey, come quickly!
Hey, where are you going?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: adjective like this

examples.trans: This kind of thing.
It is like this.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.
I want to ask right now.
How about trying to ask together tomorrow?

meanings.en: to not know, to be unaware of
meanings.note: 르-irregular verb: stem 모르- + -아요/-았어요 → 몰라요 / 몰랐어요.

examples.trans: I don't know well either.
I didn't realize time was passing.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)
